beats.text: May BHWE at trabaho na ba dahil accredited? Tanong ni Demi ito, hindi patunay ng kaniyang qualifications.
Apat na pangkat: akreditasyon, edukasyon tungo sa degree, limang qualifying years ng voluntary, continuous at full-time service, at satisfactory record. May detalyadong CSC conditions.
Sa fictional Card A, walong total years ngunit tatlo lamang habang accredited. Hindi idinadagdag ang pre-accreditation service. Huwag gawing approval ang practice card.
Maaaring kwalipikado pa rin ang JO/COS worker; hindi sapat ang label. Ihiwalay ang honorarium at allowances sa salary, at itanong ang aktuwal na arrangement sa CSC.
Tanong ni Demi: aling accredited-service period at education at service evidence ang dapat tiyakin? Sa CSC office na may sakop sa barangay ng serbisyo magtanong.
Ipaliwanag ang kondisyon, saka tiyakin sa CSC. May first-level exceptions ang BHWE; hindi ito license o garantisadong appointment. Magsanay, huwag mangako.
Does accreditation already mean BHWE and a job? Demi asks; her qualifications are not established.
Four groups: accreditation, education toward a degree, five qualifying years of voluntary, continuous full-time service, and a satisfactory record. CSC conditions provide the detail.
Fictional Card A has eight total years but only three while accredited. Pre-accreditation service cannot be added. A practice card is not approval.
A JO/COS worker may still qualify; the label is insufficient. Distinguish honorarium and allowances from salary, and ask CSC about the actual arrangement.
Demi asks which accredited-service period and education and service evidence need verification. Ask the CSC office responsible for the barangay of service.
Explain conditions, then verify with CSC. BHWE has first-level exceptions; it is not a license or guaranteed appointment. Practice without promises.
